quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other cars you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: When is passing prohibited?

options.text: In a curve.
Within 100 feet of an intersection.
If your lane has a solid yellow centerline.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in curves, hills, or places where you cannot see oncoming traffic. You cannot pass within 100 feet of intersections, bridges, tunnels, or railroad crossings. You also cannot pass when signs or road markings prohibit it.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to an accident scene just to look.

questions.question: When turning right at a red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your signal and turn immediately.
Wait until the light turns green to turn.
Stop completely, let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass, then turn right when safe.
Turn on hazard lights and turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass, then turn right when safe.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a red light unless a sign says not to. You must stop completely and let all pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass before turning.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to tell drivers you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the chance of a crash. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you need extra strength to steer. Slow down and pull off the roadway to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Look only at the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on spotting problems early. Look far ahead and scan the whole road, including the sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Traffic signals.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how well you can stop. Slow down when roads are poor or slippery so you can stay in control. Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should let drivers on the public road go first.
May force their way into traffic.
Can expect other drivers to change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should let drivers on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, let cars already on the public road go first. Merge safely when there is an opening.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop and let all traffic that does not have to stop go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
A dangerous curve is ahead.
A bump in the road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers to slow down and be careful when the pavement is wet because the road may be slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you should not cross it. A broken white line means you may cross it to pass another vehicle. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bike lanes and a cyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist the same way you would pass another car. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist on regular roads. Leave at least 5 feet on higher-speed roads or when there are multiple cyclists. Unnecessary honking can startle cyclists and cause them to crash.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use a different route.
Drive the same as you would on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the one in front of you. Your car will take longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry one.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Removes the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober or reduce the alcohol in your blood.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:

options.text: Deaf.
Part of a traffic study.
Blind.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind.
questions.explanation: You must always let a blind person with a white cane or guide dog cross first. They have the right-of-way.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians of danger. If you think another car is about to hit you, honk your horn to alert the driver.

questions.question: Round signs warn drivers of:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn of a railroad crossing ahead. Drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You will need to turn either right or left.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop on the entrance ramp and wait for traffic to clear.
Drive on the shoulder until you can safely enter the main road.
Find a gap in traffic, match the speed, and merge safely.
Force your way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a gap in traffic, match the speed, and merge safely.
questions.explanation: Do not stop on the entrance ramp. Look for an opening in traffic, adjust your speed to match it, and merge smoothly. Highway traffic has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. What does this tell you?

options.text: This is a two-way road.
This is a one-way road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: This is a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines show traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass slower vehicles when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers be aware of?

options.text: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
Large vehicles need less distance to stop.
Large vehicles are quieter.
Large vehicles drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks require a longer distance to stop. Stay in a position where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: Children will know when it is safe to cross.
Children will stop at the curb before crossing.
Children may run into the street without looking.
Children will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children may run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful near children. They may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking first.
